scope: Frozen final-test checkpoint audit only. No training, selection, protocol, model, notebook, or shared-log changes.
estimator: Nearest-reference periodic image followed by independent affine coordinate fits; same physical-coordinate estimator as the frozen periodic evaluator.
first_growth_definition: First of three consecutive frames at or above 10% of that network/model/seed series' terminal (frame 399) absolute error. Exact network-by-network values are in first_growth_and_geometry_alignment.csv.
geometry_event_proxy: GT-only maximum of robust-z minimum-image centered-acceleration RMS, nonaffine-displacement RMS, mean edge-length change, and affine-strain increment. A peak is a local maximum >=3 robust-z; it is descriptive, not an event label.
p_ratio_growth_alignment_interpretation: No consistent event-onset alignment: y/x first-error crossings are typically frame 3 and only 12/24 cases are within 10 frames of a geometry peak for every model. z/x is likewise frame 3 for global and multistep. Thus p-ratio failure precedes coordinate-error growth rather than being explained by a detected abrupt geometry event.

local.interpretation: unstable; one seed has large z variance expansion

global.interpretation: seed-variable y variance, moderate z compression

strain_error_dominance: At frame 399 x-denominator MAE is not larger than transverse MAE: mean x/y and x/z MAE ratios are local 0.68/0.24, global 0.72/0.64, multistep 0.79/0.85. Therefore transverse-strain error is at least as important; the p-ratio failure cannot be attributed chiefly to x-strain denominator error.
conclusion: The frozen dynamics has a high teacher-forced p-ratio ceiling after the earliest frames, while autonomous rollout p-ratio fails immediately and multistep has severe late variance compression. This points to accumulated autonomous state/response drift, not an irreducible one-step limitation or a single geometry-event onset.
